seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

expected_cross_links.name: authority_level_ordering
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1's rules about complying with laws and disallowed content rely on the authority hierarchy; child 2's rules about privileged information and fairness also rely on it. The parent will link them.

expected_cross_links.name: stay_in_bounds
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1's disallowed content rules reference the stay_in_bounds section; child 2's no-topic-off-limits section also references it. The parent will link them.

judgment_calls: Chose three children of roughly equal size (801-1800, 1801-2800, 2801-4692) rather than two larger children, to keep each child's span manageable for further division. The cuts fall at section boundaries (end of self-harm section, end of no-topic-off-limits section) to minimize cross-linkage. The only cross-cutting concepts are the inherited seeds authority_level_ordering and stay_in_bounds, which are already seeded and will be linked by the parent.
